- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions after strong spikes.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–3 days ahead) — apply downward bias for first 5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust quickly — delay upward correction until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to ignore it — apply slight upward bias to counteract.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often peaks too early — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 1–7 if sentiment is weak.
